Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer-provided content from hosted or dedicated deployments to train our public models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement. Below I outline the retention nuances for EU-hosted tenants and some operational exceptions.

High-level assurances:
- No model-training use: Customer content (API payloads, files submitted during inference) is not incorporated into model training datasets by default. Any change to that practice requires explicit, auditable consent.
- Default retention windows (EU-hosted) — production hosted API:
  - Primary request/response logs (tenanted): 30 days by default unless customer configures a shorter TTL.
  - Short-term debugging artifacts (in-memory KV caches, transient logs): ephemeral (seconds–minutes) and not persisted to long-term storage for standard hosted tenants.
  - Snapshots/backups: periodic infra snapshots are retained for 90 days for disaster recovery; sensitive payloads are redacted from long-term snapshots and subject to the same deletion requests described below.

Operational exceptions and clarifications:
- Debug snapshots and escalation artifacts: when a customer files a support ticket that requires session reconstruction, we may create a redacted debug snapshot that contains minimal request metadata. These are retained only for the duration needed to resolve the issue (commonly 7–30 days) unless the customer requests deletion sooner.
- Audit logs: immutable audit trails for control-plane actions (who requested deletion, who approved) are retained longer for compliance reasons; these logs do not contain full request payloads.
- Dedicated & Private: for Dedicated reservations or Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), retention defaults are set per contract and can be configured to meet FinHealth requirements.

I attached a short FAQ and a retention matrix that maps artifacts to TTLs. Ben/Neha — can you add the SOC2 reference and any extra technical detail about KV cache persistence?

If this level of detail is fine, I can produce a one-paragraph cert we can sign and include in the SOW.

> High-level assurances:
> - No model-training use: Customer content ... not incorporated into model training datasets by default.

Hi Oliver — adding the low-level notes from engineering:

- KV cache behavior: for generation workloads we maintain an in-memory KV cache to improve latency across tokens. For hosted tenants, that cache is held on ephemeral worker memory and never written to the multi-tenant durable object store. If a customer enables long-lived session persistence (opt-in feature), keys are persisted to an encrypted tenant store with the tenant-configured TTL.
- Request logs vs telemetry: request/response logs are tenant-scoped and stored in the tenant's EU region buckets; telemetry (metrics, aggregated latency histograms) is aggregated and does not contain PII or full request payloads.
- Snapshots/backups: infra snapshots are taken at the VM/container level and scrubbed by redaction rules prior to being transferred into long-term object storage. We keep a chain of 90-day snapshots for recovery; deletion requests trigger a targeted sweep that removes tenant artifacts from the object store index and flags later snapshots for redaction in the next retention cycle.

Technical exceptions where content could be seen by humans:
- Support-assisted debugging: we sanitize to the greatest extent possible but may access redacted payloads in a secure environment when a customer explicitly grants access for troubleshooting. All such access is logged and requires approval.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the archive/removal sweep process.

Thanks,

Oliver / team — attaching the SOC2 summary (redacted) and a brief deletion playbook. A few audit/compliance points to call out: 

- Written assurance: we will provide a scoped written statement (on Redwood letterhead) confirming that Redwood does not use FinHealth customer content to train our public models without documented, auditable opt-in.
- Deletion SLA: upon an authenticated deletion request from an admin, tenant data removal workflows begin immediately; primary request/response artifacts are removed from active buckets within 24–72 hours, and the index sweep for snapshots/backups completes within the stated snapshot retention cycle (we can accelerate if contractually required).
- Auditability: every deletion event creates an immutable audit record with requestor identity, timestamp, and the sweep ticket id. Those audit records are retained for 2 years for compliance and will not include the full payloads.
